Honoured to be recognized by illuminem as one of the Top 10 Most Read Thought Leaders of the Year in AI.

This recognition feels especially meaningful at a moment when AI is reshaping how we think about energy, development, and sustainability. The question is no longer only how fast AI advances, but how responsibly it is powered, governed, and used to support a just energy transition.

At its foundation, the future of AI is a question of energy. Last year, AI consumed around 415 terawatt hours of electricity, more than 150 countries individually. By 2030, electricity demand from data centres is projected to more than double to around 945 terawatt hours, roughly equivalent to Japan’s entire electricity consumption today.

I have come to see this as less a story about technology than about people: whether the systems we build expand opportunity, strengthen resilience, and reach the communities that need them most. That question is not abstract when 655 million people still live without electricity and 2.0 billion people still lack access to clean cooking, even as AI places a vast new demand on the same energy systems.

The encouraging part is that AI also presents enormous opportunities to accelerate a just energy transition, from strengthening energy systems to expanding clean energy access. The challenge is ensuring these benefits are shared. Of the US$15.7 trillion AI is projected to contribute to the global economy by 2030, around 84% is expected to accrue to just three regions. A just transition means deliberately widening that circle, ensuring that the communities too often left behind are not left behind again.

At UNDP, we are working to ensure that emerging technologies accelerate clean energy access, strengthen resilience, and deliver real development outcomes for those who need them most.

Thank you to @illuminem and its global community of readers for this recognition. It is an honour to be recognised alongside Facundo Armas, Joe Romm, •Shep Hyken, Vincent Ruinet, Philipp Petry, Dr. Niladri Choudhuri, Aparna K., Monica Sanders, and Vilas Dhar. The future of AI will ultimately be defined not by how intelligent our systems become, but by whether they advance sustainable development for everyone, everywhere.
